summary: Completed one fresh, independent startup/auth and shutdown-lifetime review of the dirty implementation based on HEAD c8a1ed06a8043fe725381ccccd89779b6a3498e0, bound to the source digests in plan.json. Found one medium-severity startup cleanup defect; no other supported findings were identified within this lens.
coverage: Read the immutable brief, repository AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, startup context, workflow, invariants, focused review guidance, and the adversarial-review schema/contract. Source digests of every subject path matched plan.json when checked after source inspection.

Inspected all new source in apps/server/src/server.ts, startup.ts and readiness.ts, and the changed entry point, auth configuration/middleware, createService cleanup, domain ticker, app lifecycle/SSE routes, and VisuaService detached execution tracking.

Traced bootstrap ownership and verified-email OIDC resolution in auth/service.ts; inspected tenant/user atomic operations and the Store transaction/afterCommit machinery for PostgreSQL compatibility and preservation of existing memberships.

Traced readiness, client disconnects, response completion and pipelining, SSE abort/write behavior, shutdown ordering and deadlines through installed Hono/node-server source, Store.close, SQLite/PostgreSQL driver close, and PgEventRelay lifetime code.

Read startup.test.ts and changed domain-recheck.test.ts cases as source; inspected related auth/domain-service behavior. Examined compose.yaml host binding/readiness/grace period and README.md/docs/architecture.md claims against the implementation.

Executed one isolated, in-memory Node reproduction through real startServer with VISUA_SEED=1. Process-local prototype fault injection held executeRun and made waitForRun throw its timeout error. Recorded whether Store.close ran before execution completion, then resumed the execution and attempted SELECT 1. The process exited 0 after reporting premature close and a closed-database query error. No application source, Docker state, shared services or build caches were changed.

findings.location: apps/server/src/server.ts:108-111 (startup failure cleanup); related apps/server/src/seed/demo.ts:336-339 and apps/server/src/services/visua.ts:1367-1374
findings.mechanism: Trigger: optional demo seeding starts a detached agent, then seedDemo.waitForRun times out or later startup work fails while that execution remains active. startServer catches the startup error and immediately closes the store without draining its executions. The agent retains the service and continues its writes, recorder flushing or error handling against the closed database. This violates startup resource ownership and can interrupt the persisted agent/audit state even though ordinary stop() correctly drains executions first.
findings.evidence: Source: seedDemo starts detached runs at lines 336 and 338 and polls their persisted status with waitForRun; waitForRun throws after its 120000 ms default at services/visua.ts:1373 without aborting the execution. launch tracks a still-active promise at services/visua.ts:1350-1356. server.ts:108-111 waits only stopRechecks before svc.store.close, unlike normal shutdown at server.ts:90-92. Executed from /Users/artem/visua: node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --input-type=module with an inline module importing startServer, VisuaService and Store; the module replaced executeRun with a promise waiting on a release callback, replaced waitForRun with an immediate injected timeout, wrapped Store.close to record active execution, and called startServer({env:{VISUA_PORT:"0",VISUA_SEED:"1"},database:":memory:"}). Actual output: {"startupError":"injected waitForRun timeout","closedDuringExecution":true}, then after release {"queryAfterClose":"database is not open","running":false}. The injection shortens the existing timeout path; it does not claim an actual model or PostgreSQL timeout was exercised. Reproduction method and output are preserved in this review.json artifact.
findings.recommendation: Make startup-error cleanup own any detached work already launched: drain the active executions before closing relay/storage, with a bounded cleanup deadline and appropriate cancellation/forced-stop behavior when they cannot finish. Preserve the original startup error. Add a focused startup-failure case with an active seeded execution to verify that storage remains open until it drains.

limitations: This was one bounded, fresh native review with no inherited author transcript. It did not inspect every unrelated service method or constitute a general security review.

Full unit/integration suites, real PostgreSQL fault injection, and a real OIDC sign-in were not executed by this reviewer; their test source and relevant implementation were inspected. Integration verification belongs to the root agent.
The reproduction uses process-local fault injection and an in-memory SQLite database to force the reachable startup timeout interleaving; it did not wait 120 seconds or invoke a model provider.
The report covers the recorded plan.json source snapshot only. Any subsequent fixes require targeted re-verification by the integration owner.
